analysis:
Change set: new unregistered internal Nemotron Super local qualification bindings (text, validated-output collector, image) plus DEBUG-only test seams in EngineV2Bridge.swift. The bridge seams (lines 506-513) sit inside `#if DEBUG` (opened at 502, closed at 534), so there is no release surface. No HTTP route, registry, attestation or coordinator-protocol change is visible.

TB-007/A-001 notes:
- NemotronSuperLocalBinding.swift:150 passes cacheScope "" and cacheEnabled from the constructor. This is the T-041 latent issue reported as a finding. The image binding hard-disables the cache (`cacheEnabled: false`).
- Capability guards reject tools, response_format, logprobs and prompt_cache_key, and model ID is pinned. Token IDs are bounds-checked to 0..<131072.
- The image path charges `VisionMemoryGate` for ingress (32x body bytes), decode and feature bytes before parsing, with 8MB body, 16-image and 16384-context caps. Reservations are intentionally not released after a retained native fault.
- `settle` and `drain` join the cleanup task, so cancellation waits for work to finish.

Unverified or secondary items for integration:
- In `runAcquired` (lines 105-116), if `lease.discardUnstartedPreparation()` throws inside the catch, control skips `release.fire()` and `joinFromOutside()`. That could leak a consumer lease. This depends on external lease semantics not supplied, so it is not a finding.
- `NemotronSuperOutputCollector` records a failure but does not cancel generation, so work runs to max_tokens. This is bounded and minor.
- Plaintext prompts and images live in provider process memory, consistent with the existing T-011/T-014 posture.
- The external `NemotronSuperRequestPlan`, `NemotronSuperLocalOutput`, `Owner` and `VisionMemoryGate` implementations were not supplied.

findings.detail: `executeBridge` always submits with `cacheScope: ""` and `cacheEnabled: reusesTextPrefixes`. T-041's account isolation relies on a coordinator-authored `cacheSalt` derived from authenticated account, model build and prompt contract. Neither `run` nor `runValidatedText` accepts or forwards a scope. If an owner builds this binding with `reusesTextPrefixes: true`, every caller shares one unscoped cache namespace. The result is cross-account prefix reuse and a TTFT oracle, which T-041 says is closed for cross-account traffic. Today the route is unregistered and defaults to cold, so this is latent. Nothing in the binding prevents a later wiring to coordinator-routed traffic from silently dropping account scoping. Fix: take the coordinator-authored scope as a required parameter, or make the cache-enabled variant refuse an empty scope. Document this as a T-041 detection hint.
findings.title: Nemotron local text route can enable the prefix cache with an empty, non-coordinator cache scope
